Awareness workshop · Impersonation and phishing

Your workplace response card

Before you share information, send money or approve access:

Pausethe sensitive action.
Verifythrough a route you already trust.
Reportuncertainty or a mistake promptly.
Recoverby following the responsible team’s instructions.

Before you act

  • Identify what the request would disclose or authorise.
  • Use the known app, saved address, staff directory or established supplier record, not contact details in the message.
  • Keep the usual approval and data-sharing process, even when the request is genuine.
  • Check which session, app or device would receive access, and whether you started it.

If you already acted

  • Stop further interaction and report what happened and when.
  • Include the channel, who it claimed to be, what you did, and which device. Keep the original message if you can.
  • Never include passwords, one-time codes or tokens. Do not forward the message to colleagues.
  • For a payment, contact finance and the bank’s established fraud channel immediately.

A logo, fluent message, known account, HTTPS padlock or completed MFA alone does not validate a request. A genuine request can still require independent verification.

Seven habits from today

  1. Contact people through the directory, not through the message.
  2. Call back on a number you already have before you pay, reset or share.
  3. Go to the app or website yourself instead of using the link.
  4. Approve only what you started and recognise.
  5. No ticket you raised, no remote access.
  6. Report early, even if you are not sure.
  7. Pause, verify, report, recover.

Words to know

MFA
A second check when you sign in, such as an app prompt or a code
Session
Staying signed in after you log in, so you are not asked again
Device code
A short code that signs another device in to your account
App permission
Letting an app read or change your mail and files
